lines.text: There's a car parked at the edge of the loch. Engine running. Keys in it. And my hand is *stuck to the door.*
In the Scottish Highlands, there's an old story about the each-uisge. The water horse.
It waits by the loch, looking like the most beautiful horse you've ever seen. Saddled. Calm. Waiting for a rider.
Touch it, and your hand sticks to its skin. Then it runs into the deepest water. And it doesn't stop.
They say all that ever washes up is the liver.
Nobody rides horses anymore. So I always wondered what it would look like now.
Tonight I found out. A perfect old car, cherry red, parked right at the water. Not a scratch. Not one footprint around it.
The engine was running. The headlights pointed straight at the loch. The keys were in it.
I only meant to look through the window. I put my hand on the door.
It was warm. It was *soft.* And my palm wouldn't come off.
The door opened by itself. The seat was wet. The radio was playing water. Just... *water.*
In one of the old stories, a boy's finger sticks to the water horse. He cuts it off to get away.
I have a pocketknife. *And five fingers.*
Then the gear stick moves into drive. *By itself.*
